messages.subject: Selection for inla.posterior.sample()
parts:
Hello,

I am looking to draw posterior samples from an inla model, specifically for the prediction. I was using this line of code:

Post.Res <- inla.posterior.sample(100, res)

However, I realised this defaults to sampling from the whole model rather than the prediction stack. I gather you can use selection = list() to only sample from a section of the model but I'm not sure how to specify this? The model set up is below - if anyone could advise I would be very grateful. 

# inla model for iteration 1 (data = it)
coo <- cbind(it$xcoo, it$ycoo)
mesh <- INLA::inla.mesh.2d(loc=coo, max.edge = c(2, 4), cutoff = 1)
spde.a <- inla.spde2.matern(mesh = mesh, alpha=2, constr = T)
indexs <- inla.spde.make.index("s", spde.a$n.spde)
A <- inla.spde.make.A(mesh = mesh, loc = coo)
coop <- cbind(pred$xcoo, pred$ycoo)
Ap <- inla.spde.make.A(mesh = mesh, loc = coop)
stke <- inla.stack(tag="est", data=list(mos = it$mos),A = list(1, A), effects = list(data.frame(hab = it$hab, time=it$time), s = indexs)) # n=1080
stkp <- inla.stack(tag = "pred", data = list(mos = NA),A = list(1, Ap), effects = list(data.frame( hab = pred$hab, time=pred$time), s = indexs)) # n=108984                     # b0 = rep(1, nrow(sim_mos_pred)),
stkfull <- inla.stack(stke, stkp)
res <- inla(mos ~ hab + f(s, model = spde.a)  + f(time, model = "ar1"),
            family = "nbinomial", control.family = list(link = "log"), data = inla.stack.data(stkfull),
            control.predictor = list(compute = TRUE, link=1, A = inla.stack.A(stkfull)),
            control.compute = list(config=T, dic = TRUE, waic = TRUE))

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Selection for inla.posterior.sample()
parts:
There is no speed-gain in using 'selection' as the whole model is
sampled, and then just the selction is stored.

If you need pointwise predictions only, you do not need simulations, but
can just compute them directly.

btw, the 'eval' functon has a vignette as its pretty useful and can be a
little confusing

H
